title: Ritual stance and perceptions of effort
core_idea: Cognitive theories posit a distinct 'ritual stance' that treats ceremonial actions in symbolic and social terms rather than utilitarian ones; the study tests whether framing identical activities as ritual versus ordinary changes perceptions of difficulty and emotional experience by presenting vignettes to participants and measuring perceived difficulty and happiness during and after the activities.
tldr: Examines whether framing activities as ritual versus ordinary alters perceived costs and emotional experience using vignette-based measures with Hindu participants in Mauritius.
